statement: Matchsticks are used to build a large triangle divided into small triangles. A triangle of side 1 uses 3 matches, a triangle of side 2 (made of 4 small triangles) uses 9 matches, and a triangle of side 3 (made of 9 small triangles) uses 18 matches. How many matches does a triangle of side 10 use?

choices.misconception: I counted only the matches around the outside of the triangle, 3 x 10.
I assumed the count goes up by 6 each time, as it does from side 1 to side 2.
I used 3 x 10 x 10 / 2 instead of 3 x 10 x 11 / 2.
I added 1 + 2 + ... + 11 instead of 1 + 2 + ... + 10, then multiplied by 3.

hints: Sort the matches by the direction they point.
Every match lies in one of three directions. Count the matches lying flat, row by row, and use symmetry for the other two directions. Check your rule against sides 1, 2 and 3.
In a triangle of side n, the flat matches come in rows of 1, 2, ..., n. The same is true in each of the other two directions.

solutions.reliable: Each match points in one of three directions. In a triangle of side n, the horizontal matches form rows of 1, 2, 3, ..., n, so there are 1 + 2 + ... + n of them, and by symmetry the same number point in each of the other two directions. So the total is 3 x (1 + 2 + ... + n). Check: n = 3 gives 3 x 6 = 18. For n = 10 the total is 3 x 55 = 165. The transferable idea: count a growing figure by sorting its pieces into types, then check the formula on the small cases you were given.
solutions.elegant: The counts go 3, 9, 18, ..., increasing by 6, 9, 12, ..., so the side-10 count is 3 + 6 + 9 + ... + 30 = 3 x (1 + 2 + ... + 10) = 165.

whyOnTest: Growth patterns test finding a rule that fits every given stage, and the traps are extending the first jump or slipping by one row.
author: Devansh Sanghavi
